column1: # Every place in test code that asks which Iceberg line the build is (IcebergLine.current()), with
# why. A test that expects one thing on the reference line (LinkedIn Iceberg 1.5.2) and another on
# the default line (Iceberg 1.12) accepts a difference of the default line; such a branch is listed
# here as "difference from main", with its cause, so that every one is reviewed in one place and a
# new one cannot be added unseen (scripts/ci/check-iceberg-line-branches.py fails on a branch this
# list does not name, and on an entry whose branch is gone). Each such branch asserts a different
# value on each line, so it fails on the default line when that line answers as main again.
#   difference from main     the default line answers differently from LinkedIn main here
#   declared difference      the branch selects entries of a declared-difference list
#   one line has the feature the test is of something only one line has (format v3 metadata, the
#                            Iceberg 1.12 endpoint list); not a difference from main
#   Iceberg client version   Iceberg's own REST client differs by version on a route LinkedIn
#                            main does not have; not a difference from main
#   detection                tests the line detection itself

column4: Repeated DELETEs on one data file: Iceberg 1.12 keeps one position delete file per data file (Apache Iceberg pull request 11868), where 1.5.2 left three; the rows read are the same.
Pins the detected line to the Iceberg build version.
The detection is stable.

The Java client applies the read bridge's column defaults (initial-default from the service's config) on the reference line only; the default line's client does not overlay them, as Iceberg 1.12 refuses defaults on v2 metadata client-side.
Format v3 metadata can be built only by Iceberg 1.12 (two tests).
The test table is v3 where the line can build v3 metadata, v2 on the reference line.
Only Iceberg 1.12's REST client reads an endpoint list from the config; on 1.5.2 none is advertised.
The Endpoint class exists in Iceberg 1.12 only.

CREATE and DROP NAMESPACE: Iceberg 1.12's SparkCatalog checks existence with namespaceExists (Apache Iceberg pull request 14507), which the OpenHouse catalog refuses ("Checking if database exists is not supported"); on 1.5.2 Spark loads the namespace record. The legacy path's recorded comparison with LinkedIn main declares the same answers.

The Spark 3.5 OpenHouse catalog declares the column-defaults capability on the reference line only, so on the default line a create that requires it is refused (422 CLIENT_CAPABILITY_MISSING) unless a declaring catalog stands in; on LinkedIn main the catalog always declared it.
The same capability: on the default line the Spark catalog does not declare column-defaults, so a table that requires it is refused with 422 CLIENT_CAPABILITY_MISSING.
An RTAS that drops a column an old partition spec uses succeeds on Iceberg 1.12 (it no longer validates old specs against the new schema), where 1.5.2 refuses it.
Pins which line's catalogs declare column-defaults: the reference line as LinkedIn main, the default line not.
Format v3 tables can be written only by Iceberg 1.12.

CREATE TABLE with format-version 3 on a cluster with the switch off: Iceberg 1.12's client builds the metadata and the service stores the table at version 2 (the service answers as LinkedIn main does); LinkedIn's 1.5.2 client refuses before any request, as on main.
The format v3 types exist in Iceberg 1.12 only.
Iceberg REST routes: RESTCatalog 1.5.2 rebuilds the loaded metadata and stamps last-updated-ms (first use), and checks table existence by loading the table (second use); 1.12 does neither.
The column-defaults capability over the Iceberg REST routes: the engine catalog declares it on the reference line only (as in CatalogPluginContractTest).
View rename over the Iceberg REST routes: 1.5.2 sends it and raises the 406 as RESTException; 1.12 reads the endpoint list and refuses before sending.
View existence over the Iceberg REST routes: 1.12 asks the exists route, 1.5.2 loads the view.
A row delta that only adds delete files is named by the client: "overwrite" by 1.5.2, "delete" by 1.12 (BaseRowDelta).
View rename over the Iceberg REST routes, as in IcebergRestCatalogViewTest.
Native column defaults need format v3, which only Iceberg 1.12 writes.
As above.
